name: Hostney Migration
author: hostney

sections.description:
Hostney Migration connects your WordPress site to the Hostney hosting platform so the Hostney worker can pull your database and files automatically. No SSH access, FTP credentials, or manual exports required. Your source site stays fully operational throughout the process.

New to Hostney?

Hostney is managed hosting for WordPress, with bot protection, daily backups and the Ellie AI assistant on every plan. You can try it free for 14 days with no credit card, and this plugin works on the trial: add your site’s domain in the Hostney control panel, and the copy lands on a temporary Hostney address while your current site keeps serving visitors. Nothing changes for them until you point your domain at Hostney. On paid plans, Hostney’s team will also run the migration for you at no extra cost.

See the plans and the free trial · How the plugin migration works

How it works:

  1. Generate a migration token in your Hostney control panel
  2. Install this plugin on your source WordPress site
  3. Go to Tools > Hostney Migration and paste the token
  4. Click “Start migration” in the Hostney control panel
  5. The worker pulls your database and files automatically

What gets migrated:

  • All database tables (exported row-by-row with primary key pagination)
  • All WordPress files (transferred in chunks with checksum verification)
  • File permissions and directory structure

What gets excluded automatically:

  • The page cache and update folders directly inside wp-content (cache, upgrade)
  • Log files
  • Backup folders directly inside wp-content (UpdraftPlus, All-in-One WP Migration, and folders whose name starts with “backup”)
  • Node modules and .git directories

Folders inside your plugins and themes are always copied, whatever their name.

Security:

All requests from the Hostney worker are authenticated using HMAC-SHA256 signatures with timestamp validation and replay protection. The migration token is removed from your site automatically when the migration is over, when it is revoked in the Hostney control panel, 7 days after you connected at the latest, and when the plugin is deactivated. While no token is stored, the plugin’s REST API endpoints do not exist.

Privacy Policy

This plugin sends the following data to Hostney servers (api.hostney.com) when you click Connect:

  • Your site URL and REST API URL
  • WordPress version
  • PHP version
  • Number of database tables and total database size
  • Number of files and total file size
  • Active theme name and active plugin count
  • The plugin’s version, whether the site is a multisite network and how many sites it has, and whether its content, plugins and uploads folders are in the standard place (a yes or a short reason, never a folder path)

This data is used solely to register and plan the migration. No file contents, database rows, passwords, or personal data are transmitted during the connection step.

During an active migration (initiated from the Hostney control panel), the Hostney worker connects to your site’s REST API endpoints to read database tables and files. All requests are authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 signatures. Data is transferred over HTTPS.

For more information, see the Hostney Privacy Policy and the Hostney Terms of Service.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Hostney Migration”, then click Install Now and Activate
  2. Go to Tools > Hostney Migration
  3. Paste your migration token from the Hostney control panel and click Connect

No Hostney account yet? The token comes from the Hostney control panel, and the 14-day free trial (no credit card) is enough to run a migration.
sections.faq:
Do I need SSH or FTP access on my current host?

No. The plugin exposes authenticated REST API endpoints that the Hostney worker calls over HTTPS. No server-level access is needed on the source site.

Will my site go down during migration?

No. The plugin only reads your site’s files and database. The one thing it ever writes is its own connection token, which it deletes when the migration is over. Your site continues to operate normally throughout the migration.

What data is sent to Hostney when I connect?

When you click Connect, the plugin sends your site URL, WordPress version, PHP version, database/file size estimates, and whether the site is a multisite network or has moved folders to Hostney servers to register the migration. No file contents or database data are sent during this step. The actual data transfer only happens when you start the migration from the Hostney control panel, and it flows through authenticated REST API endpoints.

Does this plugin work with multisite?

A multisite network with more than one site cannot be migrated with this plugin: Hostney refuses it when you connect, rather than moving one site and leaving the others behind. A network that has only one site is migrated as a single site. Hostney does not host multisite networks.

My wp-content folder is somewhere else. Can I still migrate?

Not with this plugin yet. It copies the WordPress folder, so a site whose content, plugins, must-use plugins or uploads folder has been moved out of the standard place (a Bedrock-style project, a renamed wp-content, a folder reached through a link, or an UPLOADS setting) is refused when you connect, instead of arriving without its theme, plugins or media. Tools > Hostney Migration shows this under “Folders” before you connect. Contact Hostney support to move such a site.

What happens to the token when I deactivate the plugin?

The migration token and connection status are automatically deleted from the database when the plugin is deactivated.

Does the token stay on my site after the migration?

No. When the migration completes, fails for good or is cancelled, and when its token is revoked or expires in the Hostney control panel, Hostney tells the plugin to disconnect and the token is deleted. If that message cannot reach your site, the connection still ends on its own 7 days after you connected. The Tools > Hostney Migration screen then says why the site was disconnected.

Can I use this plugin with a WAF (ModSecurity, Wordfence, Imunify, Cloudflare)?

Yes. The plugin supports optional base64 encoding of request and response bodies to prevent WAF false positives on SQL or PHP content in migration data. This is handled automatically by the Hostney worker.
sections.changelog:
1.0.7

  • Fixed: files whose name contains two dots in a row (for example “Wait…what.jpg” or
    “report..old.pdf”) were refused by the file reader and never reached Hostney. Only a
    “..” folder step is refused now.
  • Changed: the file list can now be sent in pages. A very large site, or one on a slow
    disk or behind a proxy with a short timeout, no longer has to list every file in a
    single request.
  • Changed: the plugin asks WordPress for the memory limit the admin area gets while it
    serves the migration, where your host allows it.
  • Changed: tables of other WordPress sites that share your database are no longer counted
    as part of your site’s database size.
  • Added: when you connect, Hostney is told whether your site is a multisite network and
    whether its folders are in the standard place. A network with more than one site, or a
    site whose wp-content, plugins or uploads folder has been moved, is refused at that
    point instead of being migrated incomplete. The system requirements panel shows both
    before you connect.

1.0.6

  • Fixed: a plugin or theme that keeps part of its own code in a folder named cache,
    upgrade, backup or backups (Smush and Elementor among them, and many plugins that
    bundle libraries) arrived at Hostney without that folder, and the migrated site
    showed WordPress’s critical error page. These folders are now skipped only where
    WordPress keeps caches, update files and backups: directly inside wp-content.
  • Added: the file list now tells Hostney when a very large site reached the file limit,
    and which folders and files could not be read on your server, instead of leaving them
    out silently.

1.0.5

  • Security: the migration token is deleted from your site when the migration is over.
    Hostney now tells the plugin to disconnect when a migration completes, fails for
    good or is cancelled, and when its token is revoked or expires. Until now the token
    stayed in your site’s settings until you clicked Disconnect or deactivated the plugin.
  • Security: a connection now ends on its own 7 days after you connected, even if
    Hostney cannot reach your site to disconnect it.
  • Security: the plugin’s REST API endpoints now exist only while a token is stored.
  • Security: the file reader’s check that a file sits inside your WordPress folder no
    longer accepts a neighbouring folder whose name starts the same way.
  • Fixed: failed sign-in attempts by other visitors behind the same proxy (Cloudflare,
    for example) could pause a running migration for up to a minute. A correctly signed
    request is never held back by someone else’s failures now.
  • Fixed: every request was counted twice against the rate limit, and every failed
    sign-in twice against the lockout, because WordPress checks a route’s permissions a
    second time after answering it. The limit of 900 requests a minute was really 450,
    which a migration could reach and then have to wait out.
  • Changed: when Hostney asks for it, database tables are exported in key order, one
    page strictly after the last. Rows added or removed on a busy site during the
    migration can no longer shift the pages, and tables whose primary key has more than
    one column are no longer split part-way through a key.

1.0.4

  • Added: the system requirements panel now reports the size of your database.
  • Changed: a site whose database is larger than the destination hosting plan allows
    is now told so when it connects, instead of partway through the migration. Nothing
    is copied in that case, and reconnecting works once the plan is upgraded or the
    database is reduced.

1.0.3

  • Fixed: the per-IP rate limiter refreshed its own expiry on every request, so the
    60-second window never elapsed during a migration and the limit behaved as a
    one-time cap of 900 requests. Large sites were rejected with HTTP 429 partway
    through the database export.
  • Added: a Retry-After header on rate-limited responses, so the caller knows exactly
    how long to wait instead of guessing.
  • Changed: the request rate limit now applies only to authenticated requests.
    Unauthenticated traffic is handled by a separate failed-authentication throttle and
    can no longer consume a running migration’s request budget.

1.0.2

  • Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.1

1.0.1

  • Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.0

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Database export with primary key pagination and adaptive batch sizing
  • Filesystem export with chunked transfers and MD5 checksum verification
  • HMAC-SHA256 authentication with timestamp validation
  • WAF-compatible base64 encoding for request and response bodies
  • Path traversal protection with realpath validation
  • Admin UI with system requirement checks

upgrade_notice.1.0.7: Copies files with two dots in their name, sends the file list of large sites in pages, and tells you at Connect when a multisite network or moved folders cannot be migrated. Update before you migrate.
upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Fixes migrated sites that failed to load because part of a plugin (for example Smush or Elementor) was not copied. Update before you migrate.
upgrade_notice.1.0.5: Security update: the migration token is removed from your site when the migration is over, and a connection ends on its own after 7 days. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.0.4: Shows your database size in the system requirements, and reports a database that is too large for the destination hosting plan when you connect rather than after the migration has started.
upgrade_notice.1.0.3: Fixes migrations of larger sites failing with a "Too many requests" error partway through the database export. Recommended for all users.
